The review's follow-up is that `writeRecord` appends the original's own sidecar steps to the fresh envelope before the merge when that sidecar exists and is not `found.sourceURL`, with a test that the clumped record names `SRR12486983.fastq.gz`. The PAIRING fix did not do it

A mix's roles name the plain file and are copied to the clumped file's sidecar, so they name a file that is gone (`ClassifierReadResolver+TaxaCollection.swift:158-160` with `FastqIngestSubcommand+Run.swift:278-282`). A reader that matches roles by file name, which the review did not trace, would show the mix as plain single reads, the safe reading

The NAO-MGS result lists aligned reads with `view -F 0x404` (`NaoMgsResultViewController.swift:2372-2373`) and promises a "Deduplicated read count" (`:1674`). It is the same question as NVD-UNIQUE-READS-DOUBLE-COUNT, and session 2 measured it on the walk sample. Rotavirus A has 13 unique read pairs, 26 unique mates and no read on two accessions, and BIO ruled that the unit is mates, so 26 is right (`~/lungfish-phase-records/phase-3-1/rulings/BIO-NAOMGS-UNIQUE-READS-UNIT.md:101`). The row stays S3 for one latent defect. The dedup key is one mate (`Sources/LungfishIO/Formats/NaoMgs/NaoMgsDatabase+Create.swift:428-451`), so two distinct pairs that share one mate's accession, start, strand and length lose that mate, where under the ruled unit a mate is a duplicate only when its whole pair is one, as `NaoMgsDatabase+Summaries.swift:45-56` keys it. No input has met this yet. Its test is `testUniqueReadCountKeepsTwoFragmentsThatShareAMate`, which expects 4 unique reads (2 pairs of 2 mates) and gets 3 today. Extraction from a NAO-MGS result now writes each read once with `-F 0xD04` and `-N`, so the two lists can differ for a read with a secondary alignment, and the NAO-MGS fixtures hold none.

The markdup summaries count a total with `0x4` and non-duplicates with `0x404` (`BuildDbCommand+SamtoolsProvenance.swift:114-115`, `:186-187`, `MarkdupCommand.swift:383`, `:468`), which was kept by ruling since the duplicate count cancels the secondary records. A total or fraction built from them still counts alignment records, unlike `MarkdupService.swift:24`, so where a markdup summary shows it as reads it is not a read count. The review did not measure it

`build-db` writes counts and no marker of the flags that made them (`BuildDbCommand.swift:201-206`), so one project can hold a rebuilt result with new counts beside an old result with old counts and nothing says which is which. The release note's Known limit covers it in words

A pool that mixes interleaved bundles with R1 and R2 bundles is refused, and a conversion that maps it needs one recorded step per converted input, a fixed mate order and a test on all four mappers. The real obstacle is that a pool carries no read-set plan (`MappingInputResolver.swift:198` returns `readSetPlan: nil` for a pool and `MappingResolvedInputs.readSetPlan` holds one plan, `:25`). The review's design is to plan each input for separate files, record each split step (`ReadSetStep.swift:15`, `:18`) and pool R1 and R2. It is a new feature and not a 3.0 fix

The pool trusts each input's recorded counts, so an R1 and R2 bundle with unequal files, or an interleaved input with an odd record count, shifts the pairs of every later input, and bowtie2 and BBMap check no names, so the mispairing is silent where a lone bundle stops at the mapper (`MappingPooledInputs.swift:218-227`, `:229-236`). It needs a corrupt input, and the review's later fix compares the recorded R1 and R2 counts of each input before the join, as Merge Into New Bundle does (`READ-PAIRING.md:67`). On minimap2, if the last pair of one input and the first pair of the next share a read name, minimap2 groups the four records as one fragment, and the recorded reason "each keeps its pairs" is false for those four reads (`MappingPooledInputs.swift:224`). The review's later fix refuses or warns when the last name of one input equals the first name of the next

`--paired` with two inputs that each resolve to one file, such as two interleaved bundles, passes the new count check and binds A as R1 and B as R2 with no message (`MappingInputResolver.swift:212`). bwa-mem2 stops on its name check, while bowtie2 and BBMap pair reads across the two samples. The base did the same, and the new help names the rule "Bind exactly two input files"

A track that names no source applies nothing, so the previous track's rows and bar stay on screen while its build runs (`ReferenceBundleViewportController.swift:1313-1322`, the lane's Deviation 1). The numbers on screen then belong to another track, and BIO owns those numbers

The rows of the All Alignments table exclude DUP-flagged reads while the header takes flagstat `primary mapped`, which counts them, so on a duplicate-marked track the header exceeds the sum of the rows by the duplicate count. Both are measured (`MappingSummaryBuilder.swift:53`)

The Inspector's Est. Coverage multiplies idxstats records by an assumed 150 bp over the length and shows it for a one-sequence bundle (`ReadStyleSection.swift:1045-1048`, `:1288`), so for long reads it can be off by a large factor and it disagrees with the measured mean depth of the mapping table (84.58 on the walk's record). It is labelled "Est." and is older than the MAPPED-READS lane

The stored `file_info` values `mapped_reads`, `total_reads` and `unmapped_reads` in databases made before the MAPPED-READS lane still hold alignment records. No `Sources` code reads them (`allFileInfo()` has one reader, `ReadStyleSection.swift:568`, and the panel shows only `file_name` and `derivation_*`), so only someone with a SQLite shell sees them. A line in the phase records is enough

`ViewerFigureDepthTrack.load` lets the first `fetchDepth` error escape, and `fetchDepth` throws on a nonzero exit or on the 30-second samtools wait (`ViewerFigureDepthTrack.swift:61-82`, `AlignmentDataProvider.swift:672-676`). Only the second, alias-name attempt sits in `try?`, so on very deep data the whole export would fail, where it could leave the Depth track out with the one-line note. No deep dataset was tested, and the comment that 1.6 million lines read "well inside" the 30 s limit has no timing behind it (`:19-21`, S4)

The statistics counter and the reader both decode scores with the encoding of the first record (`DemultiplexStatisticsCounter.swift` `count`, `FASTQReader.swift:215-218`). The counter's first record is the input's first read and a later measure starts at the bundle's first read, so when those two reads fall on different sides of the Solexa window (`QualityEncoding.swift:126-128`, minimum 59 to 63 and maximum above 74) the stored and the measured mean Q can differ by about 31. Rare, and the same rule as every import

A record with bases but no G or C and no scores, such as an all-A/T set, is measured again on every open, and a FASTA derived bundle goes through a FASTQ reader, so an alert may show each time (`FASTQStatisticsDisplayRules.swift:22-29`)

The exact-bare route holds one statistics counter a file, each with up to 97 groups, until the in-order merge, and each group carries position histograms of up to 1000 positions of 94 bins (about 750 KB a group), so a many-worker run over long reads can hold hundreds of MB to a few GB (`DemultiplexStatisticsCounter.swift` with `FASTQStatisticsCollector.positionQualityHistograms`). The manifests now carry `perPositionQuality` and both histograms, roughly 100 to 200 KB of JSON a bundle against about 1 KB before, for 97 bundles a run (`ExactBarcodeDemux.swift:409`, `DemultiplexingPipeline+ExactBare.swift:88-90`). No time or memory of the added pass was reported, and the scan cost of a big project is unmeasured

The read table's per-read Mean Q column prints 0.0 for a read with no scores, so a FASTA read set says "No quality scores" on the cards and 0.0 in the table (`FASTQDatasetViewController.swift:32`, `:2140`). The Quality section prints mean Q, Q20 and Q30 with bars from its own struct and may show 0.0 bars for a read set with no scores (`QualitySection.swift:168-216`, not traced). `hasNoQualityScores` keys on the empty histogram alone, so a record with a mean Q above 0 and no histogram would say "No quality scores" over a counted number (`FASTQStatisticsDisplayRules.swift:31-33`, BIO to confirm that no writer stores that shape). FASTA and bridged reads store Mean Q, Q20 and Q30 as 0 (`FASTQDatasetStatistics+Sequences.swift:25`, `:94-97`), and the review's fix shape is to show "No quality scores" when `qualityScoreHistogram.isEmpty` and `readCount > 0`

The Fluidigm materializers store an invented mean Q 40, Q20 100% and Q30 100% for reads built from sequence counts, shown as measured (`ONTFluidigmAmpliconMaterializer.swift:673-678`, `ONTFluidigmSampleMaterializer.swift:451-456`). Whether synthetic scores are dropped, as the bridge now does, is to be settled with BIO-BIN

The ONT importer parses every record in Swift where the base counted lines with `gzcat` and `wc -l` (`ONTDirectoryImporter+Statistics.swift:15-27`), and the default path does it twice, one barcode after another (`ONTImportWorkflow.swift:529`, `:540`). A binned import reads each read twice (`ONTDirectoryImporter.swift:413`, `:479`, `ONTImportWorkflow.swift:530`, `:555`), and the row holds one "Measuring reads..." message per barcode meanwhile. Nobody timed a large run, and BIO and ARCH own the cost

The adopt makes its `ProvenanceRunClock()` and its `statsStartedAt` and `statsCompletedAt` at the writer call (`ExecutorRunAdoption+Bundle.swift:154`, unchanged at the current head), so every adopted record's own wall time, its statistics step's time and its `createdAt` time the assembly of the record and not the adopt, and any display or sum that reads that field gets 0.08 s for seconds of work. A Workflow lane would start the clock at the top of `adopt`, which helps new records only

A completed run under a limit records none, except Savont, and a stopped step records the stop and its limit. A stopped bwa-mem2 mapper leaves no step, since the step is built only after the call returns, so a stop records no step, no stop and no limit (`ManagedMappingPipeline.swift:607-614`, `:616-631`, `:737`, and whether the mapping run records the failure elsewhere was not traced). `MappingSummaryBuilder.swift:492` and `:521` turn a time limit into a `CancellationError`, which reads as a user cancel and gives no reason, against the rule that a watchdog says why. It is latent, since no production caller sets a limit there (`ManagedMappingPipeline.swift:224-229`)

Reassemble checks the bytes of the reads when the menu item is chosen, and the wizard runs later, so reads that change between the check and the run are used with no word. Lane COPYINPUTS checks once, in `AssemblyProvenance.reassemblyInputFiles`

`GenotypeResultViewController.swift:8680` tags a definition read from the reference the run recorded as `.bundleSnapshot`, so the label names the bundle's own snapshot where the definition came from the recorded reference

Extract skips the index and keeps one dictionary of every named ID with its lengths and one of every found ID, about 150 bytes an ID each against about 80 for the old set, so a taxon of tens of millions of reads, such as host or root, needs several times the memory of before, and a large per-read output takes minutes where the index took seconds (`TaxonomyExtractionPipeline.swift:260`, `TaxonomyExtractionPipeline+ReadCheck.swift:24-56`). Not measured, and a crash would be S1. A streamed compare removes the memory and the lane's 3.1 row removes the time

When the per-read output is missing or cannot be read, `recordedLengths` is nil and BLAST goes on with no read check, the old "submitting mate 1" fallback (`BlastService+Sources.swift:151-162`). It takes a damaged or deleted file, since results keep the output (`ClassificationPipeline.swift:886`). The review's idea is to rethrow the lookup error when the file exists, after checking that no test pins the fallback

`fragmentName` drops only `/1` and `/2` (`ReadIDMatching.swift` with `KrakenReadLength.swift:48-50`), so an interleaved bundle whose mates are named `x.1` and `x.2` or `x_1` and `x_2` would draw mate 1 only, as before the lane, and the check then refuses it with the "trimmed, filtered" words. Not verified and no test

The synthetic `<length>M` CIGAR of a NAO-MGS BAM places the mates of four reads 1 to 15 bases off, since a soft-clipped or gapped alignment has no real CIGAR (`NaoMgsDatabase+Create.swift:273-277`, `NaoMgsBamMaterializer.swift:486`, `:529`). The TSV's own fragment length differs from the span the CIGARs imply by the same count as the shift. It is not about orientation, and S3 holds until the effect on the duplicate marks is checked. The next edit of the materializer, a file of exactly 800 lines, starts by moving code out

A NAO-MGS BAM gets an invented `@SQ LN:100000` for an accession with no known length (`refLengths[accession] ?? 100000` at `NaoMgsBamMaterializer.swift:305`). It would become S1 if a coverage or depth number divided by that length, and BIO read for that and found that no coverage, depth or percent number of the NAO-MGS view divides by the BAM's `LN`, so it stays S3. The cards divide by the database's lengths, and the current importer writes the BAM at the stage, where every accession with hits already has an `alignment-extent` length, so its header holds that extent and 100000 is reached only for an accession of an older database. The harm is outside the app, since a person who copies `bams/<sample>.bam` out and runs `samtools coverage` or `depth` gets a breadth that is inflated by up to 100% over the reads' extent. No fix is required. If one is wanted later, the header can be written after Phase 5 from the `.fai` lengths with one `samtools reheader` pass per BAM, or the manual can say that the header length is the alignment extent

After any thrown failure the materializer's loop deletes the sample's BAM, so a failed forced run with rows present deletes a good BAM (`NaoMgsBamMaterializer.swift:130-134`). The strand-fix guard avoids the common case, and the path is unreachable after a purge

The words at `ExtractionDestination.swift:129-133` and `:205-208` promise that the written count equals the table's Unique Reads and the estimate. For NAO-MGS the estimate leaves out the `-N` allowlist that the extraction applies, so a NAO-MGS row's estimate can exceed what is written (`ClassifierReadResolver.swift:222-260`, the only estimate a BAM tool reaches, against `:517-521`). It was not measured on a NAO-MGS result

The provenance of an extraction made before the `0xD04` mask records `samtoolsExcludeFlags` 1028 or 1024 (`TaxonomyReadExtractionAction.swift:682`), and the replay argv `extract reads --by-classifier` has no flag for the mask, so a replay on a BAM with secondary or supplementary records writes the `0xD04` set and not the older output that held the duplicates. It is read from the code and was not run

In a coordinate-sorted paired BAM, mates that are not next to each other come out of `BAMToFASTQConverter.swift:110-113` as singletons with one name and no suffix (the paired fixture shows `ERR5069949.29668` in both mate files and `ERR5069949.114870` in the singleton file), so the FASTQ is not an interleaved pair file. How the destination records the pairing was not checked against `docs/contracts/READ-PAIRING.md`

With `includeUnmappedMates` off, the default of the pins, the unmapped mate of a mapped read is dropped (3 of the 200 records of the paired fixture), so those fragments come out as one record. The IDs do not change and it is by design. Whether the dialog offers the choice was not checked (`ExtractionDestination.swift:209-211`)

A BAM import still writes one FASTQ record for two same-name records that carry neither mate flag (`ONTBAMImportMaterializer.swift:97-106`, the `samtools fastq -F <flag>` to stdout of an imported BAM, collated first when needed). A BAM of single-end reads holds one record a name, so only a BAM with two records of one name reaches the loss

The record of a Medaka run names one `samtools fastq -F 2304 -0 -1 -2 -s` command for the FASTQ reconstruction (`ViralVariantCallingPipeline.swift:228-239`), where the converter now runs `samtools view -b -F 2304 --rf 192`, the `fastq` over that BAM and `samtools view -O SAM -F 2496`, so the recorded command no longer reproduces the output for a BAM with two unflagged records of one name

The count shown before a region or by-ID extraction is `view -c`, so it can exceed the file (a SEQ `*` record is left out of the FASTQ and a same-name same-flag repeat is written once), and the region default (`-F 0x400` or none) keeps secondary and supplementary records (`AlignmentReadExtractionStager.swift:151-161`, `:449-465` with `ExtractionConfig.swift:176-177`, `ReadExtractionService.swift:330` with `BAMToFASTQConverter.swift:263`). Counting the records written after the write would make "count equals file" true by construction, and it moves the `readCount` stubs of `BAMRegionExtractionTests`

In a region BAM that mixes flagged and unflagged reads, two flagged records of one name and one mate flag that only unflagged reads used to separate now sit side by side, so samtools writes one. A test replay gave 4 records at the base and 3 now while the count shown stays 4 (`AlignmentReadExtractionStager.swift:180-191`). It is a repeat of a read whose twin is written, and rare. The manager's note filed this corner as S4, and the BIO review of FASTQ-SAME-NAME-2 rated it S3

The manual calls NVD Unique Reads "the reads that mapped nowhere else" (`docs/user-manual/chapters/06-classification/09-novel-virus-detection.md:151`), which is not what the column counts. The words mislead without changing a result, and the manual waits for the end of the phases

The TaxTriage record's `fetchedReferences.listingFiles` names `combine/<sample>.combined.gcfmap.tsv` for every record, including a run that failed before its combine step, and the record is written at the start and never rewritten, so a methods citation can point at a listing that does not exist (`TaxTriagePipeline+Provenance.swift:411-423`). The EsViritu and TaxTriage parity pins move again when it is fixed

The install receipt rules leave three gaps. A receipt that names another folder (a database root moved or copied, for example to the scratch disk) or ended nonzero counts as no receipt, so the record says `unpinned` with no words, and Kraken2 shares the code, so a note needs a BIO ruling (`MetagenomicsDatabaseReceiptReference.swift:100-106`). A receipt that does not add up still supplies `databaseCatalogVersion`, so a version shows beside `unpinned` and the note that says the receipt cannot be trusted (`:110-112`). `pinned` is an install-time claim re-derived from the receipt, and a run-time stat of the listed files would catch a truncated or replaced file but needs a ruling, since E9 forbids reading the files (`:135-171`)

`versionValue` drops empty cells, so NVD rows that mix a stated version with blank ones read as one release, where the ruling says "when every row agrees" (`MetagenomicsImportDatabaseIdentity.swift:75-86`). Improbable in a real file

The three released keys and every other CZ-ID import parameter, the NT and NR versions included, still show as Explicit as well as Resolved Default, so a fact of the report reads as an option that the person chose (`CzIdDataConverter.swift:331`). It is released behaviour and the ruling keeps the three keys

The bundle summary's `totalMappedReads` adds the manifest counts of every alignment track, derived copies included and kinds mixed, so a dup-marked copy doubles it (`BundleManifest.swift:780-781`, `BundleSequenceSummarySynthesizer.swift:40-41`). Only the model reads it in `Sources` (`BundleBrowserSummary.swift:26`), so it reaches the stored summary and the JSON

`parseFlagstat` reads the `in total` and `mapped (` record lines and its message says "reads mapped" (`Minimap2Pipeline.swift:876-884`, `:927-940`). `rg` finds no caller outside doc comments, so it is S3, and it becomes S2 if a route revives it

With no total, the mapping header's numerator is the build's rows, which drop duplicates and QC-failed reads, while flagstat's `primary mapped` counts them, so "N reads mapped" can read lower than flagstat for a dup-marked BAM (`ReferenceBundleViewportController.swift:1379`, `MappingSummaryBuilder.swift:53`)

With two counted tracks of which one holds counts and one none, the Inspector's totals leave the empty track out and no word says so, so Total Mapped reads low for the bundle (`ReadStyleSection+ReadTotals.swift:54-56`, `:80`, where `totalsAreUnmeasured` needs zero measured tracks and `unmeasuredTracks` at `:20` could name the track in the note). UX rated it S4 and BIO set S3. A database with idxstats rows and no flagstat lines cannot give back the `*` row that `populateFromIdxstats` skips, so "Total Unmapped (alignments)" counts only unmapped records placed on a contig, which is rare and reaches only a legacy or hand-made database (`:103-104`)

The plain BAM import has four statistics gaps. A run that collected no statistics records `totalReads`, `mappedReads` and `unmappedReads` as 0 beside `statsCollected` false (`ImportCommand+BAM.swift:546-548`). idxstats runs before the index is made, so a BAM given with no index gets no counts though flagstat needs none (`:150-177`). `samtools flagstat` on a CRAM may need its reference, inferred and not run (`:570`). The note "Run the import again, and if this note returns, check that the installed samtools is version 1.9 or later" is given for every flagstat failure, a time-out or an unreadable file included, where rerunning does not help (`:680-682`). The flagstat pass reads the whole file and prints nothing after "Collecting alignment statistics..." at 0.3, so a large BAM looks as if it hangs (S4, `:149`, `:570`)

A command that gains `--time-limit` carries the limit at every lifted launch with no edit, but its provenance parameters hold the limit only if someone also wraps them in `AnalysisTimeLimit.recording`, so a record can omit a limit that the run carried (`AnalysisTimeLimit.swift:49-54`). It is S3 now and S2 when the first such command lands. The adoption pattern is repeated by hand in nine commands and nothing checks it (`TimeLimitOptions.swift:10-14`). The FASTQ import's interleave-and-compress worker runs in `Task.detached` and starts its compressor with no limit (`FASTQIngestionPipeline.swift:531-564`), so a later `--time-limit` cannot reach it and the record would name a limit it did not carry. The lane that adds the option reads `AnalysisTimeLimit.launchTimeout` before the `Task.detached` and sets it on the spec, as `NativeToolRunner.swift:441` does

A thrown stop (Cancel today, a limit once a command offers one) leaves a partial output at the requested path in six steps, and a script that ignores the exit code reads fewer reads. BAM primer trim leaves a truncated or unindexed trimmed BAM against its all-or-nothing comment (`BAMPrimerTrimPipeline.swift:119-124`, `:168`, `:178-183`, `:210-216`). `samtools markdup` writes the requested BAM directly with no `.bai` (`AlignmentMarkdupPipeline.swift:287`, `:360-361`). The BAM import sort writes `alignments/<id>.sorted.bam` in the bundle (`BAMImportService.swift:457`, `:471`). The header rewrite replaces the BAM before the reindex and its `catch` swallows every error, so a failed reindex leaves the new BAM with the old index and neither caller reports it (`BAMHeaderPathSanitizer.swift:81`, `:105-119`, `PreparedAlignmentAttachmentService.swift:239`, `BAMImportService.swift:119`). `bgzip -f` and `bgzip -d -f` write beside the input and leave a partial file next to the intact original (`NativeToolRunner.swift:803`, `:821`, `:836`, the callers' cleanup not traced). `vsearch` writes the oriented and unmatched FASTQ to their final paths and the failure path was not traced (`OrientPipeline.swift:216-234`)

ONT genotyping reuse checks only that the files of an earlier checkpoint exist, so a rerun with another signature that is stopped midway can overwrite them, and a later run with the first signature reuses a mixed sample as complete (`durableSampleCheckpointOutputsExist` near `FullLengthONTMHCGenotypingPipeline+Checkpoints.swift:366-375`). Rare and older than the time-limit lifts

`DockerRuntime.runAndWait` waits for `docker start --attach` with no limit, and Cancel stops the docker client's process tree while the daemon keeps the container running, as it did at the old 24 h limit (`DockerRuntime.swift:335`). Two timeout messages say "timed out after N seconds" with no word of a time limit and no next step, unlike the `CondaToolTimeLimit` words, and they become S3 once a command with those steps offers `--time-limit` (`ONTBarcodeDemuxGenotypingError.swift:56`, `DockerRuntime.swift:632`)

Other call sites that pass `timeout: nil` skip a person's `--time-limit`, as the by-ID extraction did, and `rg -n 'timeout: nil' Sources` lists them (the review did not run it). The by-name staging of FASTQ-SAME-NAME-2 (`AlignmentReadExtractionStager.swift`) is the one to read first. No test shows a person's limit reaching a lifted launch other than the by-ID extraction (`ReadExtractionTimeLimitTests`), so `NativeToolRunner.indexFASTA`, the `BAMImportService` sort and the Minimap2 steps are lifted on the guard alone

A stop by the limit persists a record that says why only for `kraken2 classify` (`ClassificationPipeline.swift:610-641`). Cancel leaves a cancelled record, `map` leaves `.failed` with no reason, and `extract reads`, `align` and `variants` leave words only (`ExtractReadsCommand+Events.swift:55-57`, `AlignCommand.swift:158-167`, `VariantsCommand+Call.swift:74-87`, `MapCommand.swift:258-265`). Routing a limit stop through the writer that Cancel uses, with status failed and the stop words as stderr, would close it. It sits beside TTL-RECORD-GAPS

`MarkdupCommand.swift:377`, `:383`, `:462` and `:468` count a total with 0x004 and non-duplicates with 0x404, which keeps secondary and supplementary records in a number labelled reads, while `MarkdupService.swift:24` and `:30` use 0x904 and 0xD04. For a NAO-MGS BAM the two agree, since the materializer writes single-record flags 0 and 16 and the pair flags (`NaoMgsBamMaterializer.swift:520-533`, partly read), but for an NVD or mapping BAM run through `lungfish-cli markdup` the printed total and duplicate share would count alignment records. BIO did not read what the command prints, so it is S3 until it is read, which takes `MarkdupCommand.swift:360-480`. MARKDUP-COUNTS-RECORDS above holds the same lines from the ESV review

`BuildDbCommand+SamtoolsProvenance.swift:114-115` and `:186-187` count with 0x004 and 0x404, which keep secondary and supplementary records in a number labelled reads, while `BuildDbCommand.swift:235` and `:251` and `MarkdupService.swift:24` and `:30` use 0x904 and 0xD04. For a NAO-MGS BAM the two agree, but for an NVD or mapping BAM run through `lungfish-cli build-db` the printed total and duplicate share would count alignment records. BIO did not read what the command prints, so it is S3 until it is read, which takes `BuildDbCommand+SamtoolsProvenance.swift:100-230`. MARKDUP-COUNTS-RECORDS above holds the same lines from the ESV review

The drawer of a NAO-MGS BLAST Verify run shows an orange `2 with conflicting organisms` for reads whose top hits are `Human rotavirus A` (10941) and `Rotavirus A` (28875), which are both inside the claimed taxon. With no tax IDs in the context the count compares the first words of the names (`BlastTaxonMatching.swift:119-135`). The count does not feed the badge, so only the words mislead. The fix of BIO-NAOMGS-BLAST-SCOPE removes it

The BLAST Verify popover of a NAO-MGS result offers 20 reads and the run sends 11, with no word about the gap, while the drawer's `(11 reads)` is true. The popover caps by `row.uniqueReadCount` (`NaoMgsResultViewController.swift:2278`), which counts alignment signatures, and a result with no stored hits falls back to the BAM over the top accessions with one line for each read name. The ruling's fix says `11 of 20 requested` in the drawer summary and caps the popover by read names. The ruling leaves one check open, a read-only count of the distinct read names against the table's Unique Reads of 26, which the walk's STALE W4 run read as 13 read names with 2 mates each
source: `SCR/rulings/BIO-NAOMGS-BLAST-SCOPE.md` Q4, `SCR/walk/walk-log.md` second walk and STALE W4

effect: Extract Reads on a new NAO-MGS result reads `≈ 31 unique reads` for Rotavirus A, and the extraction wrote 26 FASTQ records (13 read names with 2 mates each), so the sheet's estimate is 19% above what it writes. The table's Unique Reads reads 26 and counts mates, which is the ruled unit. The estimate sums `samtools view -c -F <mask>` over the taxon's accessions (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Extraction/ClassifierReadResolver.swift:231`, `:240-241`), so it is the taxon's own 28 records plus the 4 records of taxon 10941 on the shared accession KP198630.1 minus the 1 record that carries the duplicate flag, while the extraction writes the taxon's own reads. The gap comes from scope and the duplicate flag and not from the unit (`~/lungfish-phase-records/phase-3-1/rulings/BIO-NAOMGS-UNIQUE-READS-UNIT.md:90`, `:104`)

A NAO-MGS row with a tax ID of 0 or less passes no accepted tax ID (`ViewerViewController+NaoMgs.swift:112`), so the older first-word rule judges and counts "Rotavirus C" as supporting "Rotavirus A" (`BlastService+Verdicts.swift:288-294`). NAO-MGS rows carry real tax IDs, so it is rare

The NAO-MGS import summary says "N reads" with N the number of NAO-MGS rows, which are read pairs for paired-end input (`ImportCommand+NaoMgsNvd.swift:124`), so the CASPER fixture prints 35 while the viewer's Hits sum is 68. `NaoMgsCommand.swift:132` and `:437` ("Total hits", "Total virus hits") count rows too. The import provenance key `totalHitReads` records the same row count (`MetagenomicsImportService.swift:929`), so a reader who takes it for reads gets half the Hits sum for paired-end input. Name the unit ("read pairs") or print the mates

In NVD's By Taxon grouping, two or more grouping rows selected alone reach the multi-selection bar, which enables Extract Reads. The selector builder skips `.taxonGroup`, so the selectors are empty, the guard returns and the button does nothing and says nothing, and a mix of grouping rows and contigs reads "N rows selected" while the dialog counts only contigs (`NvdResultViewController.swift:1636`, `:2750-2753`). To see it, open By Taxon, Shift-click two taxon rows and press Extract Reads. Later fix is to grey Extract with the R4 words when no contig is selected

The EsViritu words for a missing alignment file (R10) fire only when the database records no BAM path. A recorded path is kept with no file check (older databases keep absolute paths), so a moved BAM goes on to the extraction (`ViewerViewController+EsViritu.swift:270`) and fails with the extraction service's words through `drawer.failure` (`:172-175`), which were not read. Nothing is sent to NCBI either way, and those words may not say so (`EsVirituResultViewController.swift:596-603`, `ViewerViewController+EsViritu.swift:90-93`)

`try? db.fetchReadNames` reads a thrown query as an empty set, so the selector drops its read-name allowlist and the extraction goes by accession and tax ID, which can take other taxa's reads aligned to the same accessions. An empty list is also the designed answer for merged results, so the dialog cannot tell the two apart (`NaoMgsResultViewController.swift:1871`)

`while sqlite3_step(stmt) == SQLITE_ROW` ends on any non-row result, so a statement that fails to run reads as no rows or as the rows so far (`NaoMgsDatabase+Queries.swift:399`, `:78`). The viewer then sends fewer reads to BLAST or takes the BAM route with no words. It was seen once, in the first form of a test where `fetchVirusHitsForBLAST` returned no rows after the table was dropped under an open handle, and a real trigger is rare

X/Y verified does not say how the Y reads were chosen, so a subset by position or by best match can read as a taxon-wide check. EsViritu draws the first 5,000 reads in BAM order (`ViewerViewController+EsViritu.swift:256`, `:278`), the NAO-MGS BAM route takes the first unique names for the top accessions (`NaoMgsResultViewController.swift:2330`, `:2404`) and its database route takes the lowest edit distance first (`NaoMgsDatabase+Queries.swift:385`)

BAM routes sample mates, and a chosen longest mate's sibling leaves the pool (`BlastService+Subsampling.swift:82-85`). After BLAST-MATES the words show it. Trigger is a large row whose fragment count misleads a reader

The NAO-MGS fallback sends the first record of a name, whichever mate that is. One read is sent and one judged, so it is honest. Trigger is a saved NAO-MGS result with inconclusive reads whose other mate matches. Saved records so far read 18 of 18 verified

Neither `search.taxonomy` nor `lineage` in a saved BLAST record names the taxonomy build. The accepted IDs are in the record and the CLI command, so the verdict can be reproduced without the build, but a reader cannot say which build chose them. Add it at the next schema change. For the same reason a hit filed under a node newer than the local dump falls to the name rule (the dump on the walk Mac is dated 2026-10-09). BLAST-ESVIRITU-TABLE-IDENTITY joins this row

An imported EsViritu result, with `databasePath` `/imported` (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Metagenomics/MetagenomicsImportService.swift:105`), on a Mac without the EsViritu database keeps names only, so it is judged by names. The `Name` route could serve if `Name` and `species` must agree on one species. Trigger is an owner or user report on an imported EsViritu result

Some species-rank nodes are catch-alls such as `Polyomavirus sp.` and `Hepacivirus sp.`, and a few EsViritu tax IDs lie under them. If such a node has unrelated children, the species-level rule accepts them all, the false Supported direction. For EsViritu rows it is measured and closed (79 roots, 152 accessions, 0.5%, at most 2 descendants each). It stays open for NAO-MGS, NVD and TaxTriage claims, which nobody has measured. Trigger is a saved supporting read whose top hit shares only such a root

A hit outside the clade IDs counts as clade when its organism holds the row's name or a path name as a whole phrase (`Sources/LungfishCore/Services/Blast/BlastTaxonMatching.swift:96-99`), so records of another NCBI species can support a row (710 of 7,190 EsViritu rows, 28% of accessions). The same step serves NAO-MGS, TaxTriage and NVD claims, unmeasured there. Trigger is a saved supporting read whose top hit sits in another species at 90% or more through the name alone

The saved `search.taxonomy` holds IDs and names but not the EsViritu table's version or path (`Sources/LungfishIO/Formats/EsViritu/ViralDetection+BlastVerification.swift:38-47`), so an import judged through another version's table cannot be told from a native run. It joins BLAST-TAXONOMY-BUILD-IN-RECORD for the next schema change

In the exported BLAST table the no-hit mate of a supporting or contradicting fragment carries the fragment's Taxon Check word beside blank hit columns and a Verdict of `unverified` (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/ViewerExport/BlastVerificationTableExport.swift:65-67`, `:69-87`), so a reader who counts rows and not read IDs overcounts. The notes line should say the word is per read ID
The `errorMessage` of an `.error` read (set at `BlastService+Verdicts.swift:109`) is not written (`BlastVerificationTableExport.swift:62-87`), so the exported file reads `error` with no reason
The contig and sequence drawers hide the status column (`Sources/LungfishKit/BlastResultsDrawerTab.swift:1385`, `:1391`), yet the export writes a Verdict column for them that the person never saw

An NVD hit with no integer adjusted tax ID has tax ID 0 and an empty clade (`NvdBlastHit+BlastVerification.swift:30-32`, `:63`), so the export says `no taxon queried` while the verification drawer shows counts judged by name against `classificationName`. A clade of its name, as TaxTriage builds at `TaxTriageOrganism+BlastVerification.swift:28-30`, would fix it but changes verdicts

A legacy archive saved with no request and tax ID 0 (an old EsViritu verification, if any exist) reads `no taxon queried` in the export though it was judged by name (`BlastVerificationTableExport.swift:132-135`)

Run Again's index falls back to the held index (`TaxTriageResultViewController+BlastRestore.swift:65`), so a sample with a BAM entry and no index entry could pair its BAM with another sample's index once a sample segment is chosen. Not shown. The batch handler resolves it from the BAM (`TaxTriageResultViewController.swift:2043-2044`)

Each click decodes every record in the folder before it tests the match (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Metagenomics/BlastVerificationArchive+SavedSearches.swift`, `newestSubmission`), and in 12S every `updateActionBar()` starts such a scan, including each filter keystroke (`TwelveSAmpliconResultViewController.swift:1516`). The scan runs off the main actor and the next click cancels it, so it only delays, but a project with many large searches means disk reads while arrowing. Idea is to test the lineage before decoding the result. UX rated it S4 and BIO S3
A saved record whose `query.fasta` is missing or unreadable never restores and says nothing (`BlastSavedSearchRow.swift`, `query(ofRecordAt:holds:)`), so a search the person ran can seem lost

The loader still reads a missing unresolved table as no sequences (`Sources/LungfishIO/Bundles/TwelveSAmpliconResultBundle.swift:158-161`), so `lungfish-cli fastq 12s-export-unresolved` on a damaged bundle gives zero sequences with no word that the table is missing, though the viewer now says so (lane STALE12S, Fix C). The lane rated it S4. A silent zero is a number a CLI user may trust, so BIO rates it S3, and it is rare since it needs a damaged bundle

A metadata import replaces the bundle's run record with its own (`Sources/LungfishApp/Services/SampleMetadataBundleImportService.swift:58-154`, which writes the caller's envelope over `.lungfish-provenance.json`), and a metadata edit appends a step to that record and writes it again (`persist`, `:262-374`). After an import the 12S run's argv, times and tool versions are no longer in the file, so anything that reads the bundle record as the 12S run's would find the import. `verifyTwelveSAmpliconBundleProvenance` runs only after an app run, so it is not hit. This is why lane STALE12S compares a table stamp and not the run record, and the lane did not follow the finding further

After a 12S result is replaced on disk while it is open, the screen keeps the old numbers and only the actions stop. Export refuses in words and BLAST refuses when its query is not the rows on screen (lane STALE12S), and a person can still read numbers off the old screen until they select another item in the sidebar and then the result again. The release notes say so in a Limit. The ruling rated the stale pane alone S3 and said a later row can make the viewer notice a replace by itself. It left a watcher out of the fix, because a watcher would be wider and would leave the sidebar-on-a-folder state and the reload-during-write state open

The path names that lane BLAST-LINEAGE adds to a claim's species clade are held whole by a record of another species for 243 of 17,662 viral candidate names, 1.4% (`Sources/LungfishIO/Formats/NaoMgs/NCBITaxonomyLineage.swift:56-71`). A verified top hit in such a record counts as supporting for a claim below the name, for example a bat betacoronavirus 1 record for a Human coronavirus OC43 claim. Trigger is a saved supporting read whose top hit sits in a record of another species and only in a path name. A narrowing needs the context to know which IDs the dump holds, so it is not for now. The review found no capture on the walk's Human rotavirus A row, whose 35 hits all carry 10941, 28875 or 3432193

For a hit with no tax ID the name rule is a plain substring (`Sources/LungfishCore/Services/Blast/BlastService+Verdicts.swift:213-216`), so the new path name `Mamastrovirus 1` also takes `Mamastrovirus 10`. BIO-BLAST-WALK Q2 item 6 already plans `containsPhrase` there. No saved record holds a hit with no tax ID

A claim on a merged tax ID reads nil from `speciesClade` and keeps `[taxId]`, for example SARS-CoV-1's 227859, merged into 694009 (`NCBITaxonomyLineage.swift:34`), and a hit filed under a node newer than the dump falls to the name rule. BIO-BLAST-WALK Q2 item 2 adds `merged.dmp` for the EsViritu lane

The table and strip of an assembly viewer keep the old rows and statistics after the contigs file is replaced on disk, until a person selects another item in the sidebar and then the result again (`AssemblyContigCatalog.swift:56-58`, `:151-153`, `SidebarViewController.swift:1732-1734`). Fix A of ruling BIO-ASSEMBLY-REPLACED stops every action and the pane, so the table alone can send nothing and write nothing, as the stale 12S screen does (TWELVES-STALE-SCREEN). The release notes carry it in the Limit 12S results

Narrowed in 3.2 (9b3f47634, d7fdad850). A search now asks NCBI for 500 records when a claim holds tax IDs, a shared tie shows its first clade record first, and the record keeps the tie summary and the database sequence count. Why a list of 5 and a list of 500 kept different best scores at NCBI is not explained. One case, for BIO-BLAST-TIES. On rota7 read `2129:11905:11145`, a list of 5 had a best bit score of 261.5 and a list of 500 a best of 256.0. A wider list should not lose the best record, so either the list size changes what NCBI keeps or a run can miss it. If real, a read's verdict can change with the list size

A replaced FASTA of the same layout and length reads the new bases under the old annotations, variants and alignments, and no reader can see that without a stamp. BIO rates it below the short read, since LGE then returns exactly what the file holds at the index's coordinates and the person made the change. It rests on reading and on one measured case (V3 in the ruling), and was not run at equal length. An mtime check would falsely refuse a copied project, so a stamp means a checksum in the manifest

Planned 3.2, as the rulings set (O130). A person cannot search a database of their own, so reads with private data must leave the Mac for NCBI or go unchecked, and every search depends on NCBI's queue. `blast submit --database` takes only an NCBI database name, the app offers no choice, and `BlastServiceEndpoints.swift` names no other host by design. `blastn` is managed in the `full-length-mhc-genotyping` pack. A narrow database repeats the false Supported of BIO-NAOMGS-BLAST-SCOPE, so BIO rules first

An import of a batch made before Phase 3.2 reads Not recorded for its negative controls and run settings, yet the sample folders it holds still carry their own sidecars, and those could give the marks back. Left out of lane TTIMPORT, which does not change older folders at read

With a selection, an unticked ordinary sample has a blank column in the organism matrix and a `0 organisms` line in the batch report, as at the base (`TaxTriageBatchExporter.swift:143` and `generateOrganismMatrixCSV`), and a reader takes the blank for a sample with nothing found. BIO asks for the words `not in this export`. Fix 1 of lane TTCONTROLS corrected the line for a control only, and the words are absent at `8312f57a9`

`TaxTriageResultViewController.swift:3013` still builds `TaxTriageControlMatch` with `failedSampleIDs: []` (standing at `8312f57a9`), so a failure would be hidden if the helper were reused for words. No person meets it today

A plain result folder whose record names a file at its run level with bytes that no step of the record accounts for is refused, and so is an import whose `_temp/*` files are gone. Examples are the 67 sample folders of `taxtriage-batch-*` from 2026.10.4 to 2026.10.22, whose BAM grew after the record, and an `esviritu.sqlite` another program rewrote. The refusal is true and the original stays where it is, so waiting loses nothing. A silent copy would carry a record that vouches for bytes it never saw, and a copy with a note needs a new field and a reader

`rewriteSelectedOutputDescriptors` (`GUIImportedProvenanceRehydrator.swift` about `:251-326`) drops every output whose path is not mapped from the copy's record, so an entry such as `pipe:stdout:samtools-sort` is in the source's record and not in the copy's. The copy itself is whole (`testAPipeEntryDoesNotRefuse`)

A `lungfish*` bundle's record is not compared with its files. The service hashes each payload file in source and copy (`NativeProjectCopyImportService.swift:98-111`), so the copy equals the source, but a bundle whose file changed since its record copies without a word and the copy's record repeats the old claim. The first step is `testABundleWithAChangedFileAndARollupRecord`, which flips one byte in a bundle file listed in the rollup and copies it, and if the copy's record then names digests its files do not hold, BIO looks again

A run whose own database build failed, then opened, then copied. The build marks the BAM (`BuildDbCommand.swift:142`) and leaves the run's record alone (`BuildDbCommand+Provenance.swift:228`), so the run level names bytes that are gone. The cure appends the build's steps to the run's record and passes its run level through `presentBytes`, with the test `testABuildAfterTheRunNamesTheMarkedBAMInTheRunRecord` in LungfishCLITests

Only the first read decides whether a file is rewritten (`MappingDottedMateStream.swift:33-38`, `firstReadIsDotted`), so a mixed file that starts with a lone read in another naming form is not rewritten and the record says `mapped as pairs` over 0 paired reads

bowtie2 and BBMap BAMs keep `SRR1.7.1` and `SRR1.7.2` as the two names of a pair flagged properly paired. LGE's mapping runs no fixmate or markdup (`rg` of `Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Mapping` finds none), so its numbers hold, and a viewer or `samtools fixmate` pairs by name. Not checked in the viewer

An R1/R2 pair under unreadable names records `0 / 0 / N` beside `pairing: interleaved` (`FASTQBatchImporter+RecordedReadCount.swift:39-40`), a count that outlives a later widening of the rule. A guard on `scan.matePairs == 0` would keep ruling 2 for non-dotted forms, and BIO decides

A form `under.7_1` and `_2` gives Kraken 2 20,000 for 10,000 pairs with no warning, and minimap2 and bwa-mem2 print `mapped as pairs` over 0 paired reads (`measure-after.log:17,23,29` of the lane, `MappingTool+ReadLayout.swift:39,51`). It is a false number with no warning on a form the reviewer thinks rare, and if a real `_1` and `_2` interleaved dump turns up BIO raises it to S1
A stated `--read-format interleaved` on a mixed file counts 140,000 where the auto route counts 80,000 (`measure-after.log:63`), and no key in its provenance says it ran unpaired
A 3-read SRA spot dumped with `--split-spot --readids` pairs reads 1 and 2 and leaves read 3 single (`FASTQReadLayoutClassifier.swift:64-66`)

`unmergedPairs` is the pairs that passed fastp's filter less the merged reads (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Recipes/RecipeToolReportCounts.swift:25-29`), so a pair that fastp's filter removed is in neither number and `dropped N pairs that did not merge` can be fewer than the pairs the import lost. BIO named these counts and decides whether the sentence needs the filtered pairs too

Only the first file is checked, because the route passes `fastqURL` only (`FASTQDatasetSurface.swift:133`, `MainSplitViewController+GenomicsDisplay.swift:342-350`), so a paired or multi-file bundle whose second file is gone or locked still opens with the stored numbers of both. The fix passes `resolvedFASTQURLs` in `Input`

Stored statistics are not stamped against the file (`MainSplitViewController+GenomicsDisplay.swift:340`, `cachedStatisticsMeta`), and only the in-memory copy is (`:334-339`), so a FASTQ replaced under the same name by hand shows the old numbers. It would be S2 if any LGE operation rewrote a FASTQ in place, which BIO did not check. It is the FASTQ counterpart of REFERENCE-GENOME-NO-STAMP

A contigs file that opens and does not parse leaves the viewer open with the sidecar's numbers over an empty table once REPLACED's alert is dismissed (`Sources/LungfishAssemblyUI/AssemblyResultViewController.swift:680-684`), the half-truth the head removes for a file that is gone. The words exist and the behaviour is the base's

The route's catch (`updateAssemblyDocument(nil)`, `Sources/LungfishApp/Views/MainWindow/MainSplitViewController+ContentDisplay.swift`) clears only the assembly's own block, so an assembly that does not read, selected after a Kraken 2 or FASTQ row, leaves that row's Inspector numbers beside a status line about another item. The same as the base. The lane filed S4 and BIO set S3, since the numbers shown belong to a different result

A second opening of the same result while the first edit waits shows the file without the waiting comment or review, and a waiting review changes the calls the matrix infers, for the length of one workbook update (`ViewerViewController+Genotype.swift:47` builds a new controller each time, `GenotypeResultViewController.swift:1209`). Base behaviour

A publication lock that never clears keeps the retained controller, its loaded result and a 350 ms timer for the life of the process (`GenotypeResultViewController.swift:2100-2103`, `MainSplitViewController+ContentDisplay.swift:535-538`). It needs a cap or a stale-lock check

The Judged At cell of the BLAST table export holds `species`, `rowTaxId`, `names` or blank under a header that reads as a time, and `rowTaxId` can read as the stricter reading (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/ViewerExport/BlastVerificationTableExport.swift:70`, `:78`). Plain words in the file or a legend in the `blast export-table` help would close it. UX rates S4 and BIO S3

`paneIsOn` is true when the run's row or the pane's row is nil, so a verdict can land unnamed on the open row (`Sources/LungfishKit/Classifiers/ClassifierResultActions.swift:397`, now `paneIsOn` at `:406`, body not re-read at `8312f57a9`)
`No result is saved until one comes back` is untrue in the window between a publish and a stop (`Sources/LungfishKit/BlastSearchPaneState.swift:145-146`, `.stopped`, standing at `8312f57a9`)
The source stamp of a saved BLAST search hashes a file that an extract or an export may rewrite, which was not verified

A stated layout that a scan outranks assembles single where no statement gives `-1 -2 -s`, so the contigs are weaker, with no false pair (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Assembly/AssemblyReadSetResolution.swift`, `resolved(...)`, and `Sources/LungfishApp/Views/Assembly/AssemblyConfigurationViewModel.swift:414`). 3.2 made the assembler's words say that the true pairs add no paired-end links and to run again without the stated layout (`0bdd96cef`), and the behaviour stands. `AssemblyRunRequest.resolveInputLayout` on three execution files is unread, so a fix agent reads it first

A request for interleaved handling that a scan refuses runs Kraken 2 single where auto gives pairs beside single reads, so fragment and pair-side counts run high (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Metagenomics/ClassificationPipeline+ReadSets.swift:83-90`). 3.2 changed the words so that both reads of a true pair count and `--read-format auto` counts pairs beside single reads (`88b08228c`), and the record names the scan (`cb569f1ed`). How a stated `--read-format` reaches it through the planner was not traced

A shuffled file is told it `mixes merged reads with pairs` (`Sources/LungfishCLI/Commands/FastqDeinterleaveSubcommand.swift:45-48`), and following the words gives 1 pair and 139,998 single reads, exit 0, from 70,000 true pairs. No false pair, but the words mislead

`FASTQReadLayoutClassifier.countMates` was timed only in Debug on 140,000 records, about 107,000 records a second, so the ruling's bound of about 7 minutes per 100 million records is unproved. It should be timed in release on 2,800,000 records with the candidate

Scan fields sit in the canonical envelope and not in the persisted sidecar (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Mapping/ManagedMappingPipeline.swift:208`), so a mapping record rebuilt from its sidecar holds none. A known limit that report 4 of lane READLAYOUT names
A sidecar saved before its FASTQ exists is not written (`Sources/LungfishIO/Formats/FASTQ/FASTQMetadataStore.swift:80-84`), so its count is lost and the next run scans. No false fact

Copy Row as TSV leaves out Unique Reads (`ViralDetectionTableView.swift:952-957`, `:967-972`), while the export now writes it beside Read Count (`ddcdfe51d`). From round 1 of the ESVUNIQUE review, and not rechecked at the head
A FASTA list with no file or several files records a stale or first-file source for its BLAST search, so its row can miss the saved search (`ViewerViewController.swift:1343-1349`)

A BAM with duplicate-flagged reads shows contig rows that sum below the summary bar with no word, and samtools older than 1.9 puts record counts on the bar (`MappingSummaryBuilder.swift:53`, `ManagedMappingPipeline.swift:1094-1118`)

For a gone BAM the warning says `Open the mapping again to try once more`, which cannot help (`ReferenceBundleNumbersConformanceTests.swift:87-90`). BIO asks for a file check first and words that name the BAM
A failed mapping open leaves the last result's Provenance target, selection and Alignment block (`MainSplitViewController+ContentDisplay.swift:940-944`)

W-23. The Unique Reads of a paired-end NAO-MGS run count mates (8 for 4 read names), and so does the export's `unique_read_count`, though the verdict counts what was sent. BIO rated that mates are reads, so the count is not false, and whether the column's word is right is open. The dialog's `Reads to submit` half is held by NAO-BLAST-COUNT-WORDS and NAOMGS-BLAST-READ-COUNT

An assembly whose contigs file was emptied after its record was written (zero bytes, stored statistics that count contigs, outcome `.completed`) is not refused, so the strip shows the stored Contigs, Total bp and N50 over an empty table with no alert, the W-30 symptom by another route (`AssemblyResultViewController.swift:511-514`). A refusal when `statistics.contigCount` is above 0 and the file has no bytes would close it. Rare, and unlike ASM-CONTIGS-UNPARSED-KEEPS-NUMBERS no alert shows

A TaxTriage result with only the legacy confidence table (`multiqc_confidences.txt`, no organism report) is never called stale (`TaxTriageDatabase.swift:62-66`), so its old counts and its primary accession alone stay for the counts and for all three reference actions until a `--force` build. Old pipeline versions only

A row whose BAM is missing, or whose samtools call fails, keeps its parsed ODR count, yet the mark says `organism_references` (`BuildDbCommand.swift:223-225`), so the mark says which references the pass named and not which number is shown. BIO's finding F1 of the TTREADS review decides

An accession listed under two organism names of one sample is kept for the first by `organismOf` and listed under both by `accessionsOf` (`BuildDbCommand+TaxTriageCore.swift:249-259`, `organismAccessions(in:)`), so both rows count its reads. Rare

A TaxTriage row whose ODR organism spans several gcfmap organisms gets the first one's references for Extract Reads, BLAST and the pane, and counts Unique Reads on those references only, since the grouping uses the gcfmap's organism name (`BuildDbCommand.swift:618`, `BuildDbCommand+TaxTriageCore.swift:267-279`) while TaxTriage sums strains into one row (`match_paths.py:2733`). Reads is the report's own cell, so it is not touched

TaxTriage's Unique Reads counts before TaxTriage's MAPQ floor (`match_paths.py:936`, `nextflow.config:72`), so where it shows it describes a wider set than Reads. Counting with `-q` at the run's floor would fix it once the run's parameters are known

A TaxTriage report with neither the `# Reads Aligned` nor the `Reads Aligned` column, or with a non-numeric cell there, gives Reads 0 through `?? 0` (`TaxTriageOrganismReport.swift:219`), and since Reads is now the report's own cell the BAM pass no longer covers that case. A nullable `reads_aligned` that shows a dash would say that the count is not recorded. No batch of the walk shows such a report

A TaxTriage result in the state that fix round 5 keeps safe cannot be recounted by the app, which shows `Build failed` with the new words and then the not-shown words. Carrying the old Kraken-only rows of such a sample into the rebuild would end that, and it is a later lane

A TaxTriage batch in which no sample wrote a taxonomy report gets no `taxtriage.sqlite`, and the CLI line promises that LGE builds it when the result opens (`BuildDbCommand+TaxTriageCore.swift:607`, `ClassificationCompletionDetail.swift:74`), which cannot hold for that cause. How the viewer behaves on such a result is unchecked, and so is the batch report's wording for a control that finished with no organism. BIO decides the words

When idxstats fails at build, no reference has a length or support, so the alignment pane falls back to the BAM parse and opens the first accession by name, segment 4 for Influenza again (`TaxTriageResultViewController.swift:1816-1837`, `displayTaxTriageMiniBAM`). Rare

`group.flatMap { $0.accessions }` goes to samtools with no repeat check (`ClassifierReadResolver.swift:231`, `:493`, `:524`), so a command line that names one accession twice, or two selectors of one sample with overlapping lists, still asks for a region twice, which can write a read twice (by the samtools manual, not run). The viewer no longer does it

Two folders of one batch that hold the same sample name give one id the paths of both, and the first file that exists wins, which may be the other run's (`ClassifierReadResolver+RecordedBAM.swift:45-46`, `TaxTriageResultViewController.swift:2881-2884`). The viewer keys requests by sample name too, so the table cannot tell them apart. An app-made batch names its folders by sample, so it is not shown reachable

severity: S3 leftover (the S2 is closed by LAND-30), a Known limit
effect: The matrix and the results table of a TaxTriage result made before 2026.11.1 do not say that two sample names became one; the left-out sample has no column, and an organism that only a left-out control held reads No. The viewer and the batch report say it (technical record Known limits, TaxTriage sample names). A salmon plan refuses a bundle that holds its pairs interleaved in one file, in words (`SalmonPlan+Reads.swift:13,31`). `STARPlanSubmit.swift:46` picks the request fit by `assembly.name` alone, while the fit holds for `--genomeSAsparseD 2` and memory follows the index. The disk estimate of a STAR plan uses 140 bytes a pair, the gzip rate (`STARPlanSubmit.swift:26-28`). A plain FASTQ pair is about 500 bytes, so the estimate runs about 3.5 times high, and a plain sample of about 50 M pairs or more asks past the 150 GiB slot and waits unmatched. A person's `millionPairs` overrides it where the CLI passes one (M3)

The STAR GeneCounts adopt keeps column 2 of `ReadsPerGene.out.tab` (unstranded) as the one gene table of every result, since no plan records the library's strandedness (`STARPlanRequest` in `STARPlanTypes.swift:71-85` has no strand field) and the chain counts unstranded (`STARPlan+Pipeline.swift:31-33,42-43`). A person with a stranded library therefore gets the unstranded count, a true count by a named rule, and no count by strand. BIO's ruling has the adopt name the column in the route's `geneCountsColumn` words, warn when the strand share is below 0.4 or above 0.6, and keep the whole file under `source/<sample>/` so columns 3 and 4 stay readable. Every library measured is unstranded (strand share 0.498 to 0.511 on 10 files), and on the seven real runs a wrong column would change about half of each gene's count on 17,000 to 22,000 genes a run, which would be S1, so no adopt picks column 3 or 4 until a setting exists. The fix is a plan setting `strandedness` (unstranded, forward, reverse) that the adopt maps to column 2, 3 or 4 and whose other values it refuses in words. EX-PLAN-STAR takes it (lge-lane-opus, BIO review).

The operation sheet titled "MiSeq Amplicon MHC Genotyping" has an Overview that reads "Genotype one ONT barcode FASTQ by exact full-amplicon mapping, retained-read barcode demultiplexing, and Excel reporting." Title and Overview are both keyed on the tool case `.ontGenotyping` (`FASTQOperationDialogState.swift:1959` and `:1222-1223`), so a person who picks this MiSeq tool for Illumina reads is told it takes one ONT barcode FASTQ. The walk of the 2026.11.10 candidate saw it on the sheet opened from the Operations list with S-1 selected. No result changes. The same sheet also asked for a Barcode Definition ("Required before this tool can run") and its footer read "Select a reference sequence to continue." while the reference pop-up showed one. That walk ran in background control, rated neither, and could not say whether prepared Illumina bundles need a Barcode Definition. The fix is an Overview that says what the tool does for Illumina amplicon reads, and a walk with the app in front settles the other two.

`STARIndexRecordStore.find` reads an `index-record.json` that is not valid JSON and throws the decoder's error (`STARIndexRecordStore.swift:56`). `CLIFailureWords.describe` has no case for a decoding error and gives its `localizedDescription` (`CLIFailureWords.swift:22-30`), which names no file (read, not run). `index-adopt` reaches it, since `write` calls `find` first (`STARIndexRecordStore.swift:84`), so a person with one damaged record file in the store sees a bare error and is not told which file to remove. Only a hand-edited or damaged file reaches it, and the base behaved the same way. STAR-STAGED-INDEX-RECORD-FEW-FILES-PINS notes the same bare error in passing. The fix throws a refusal that names the file and says to remove it and adopt the index again, as the words for a schema above 2 do (`STARIndexRecordStore.swift:53-54`), and a test writes a record file holding `{` and expects the file's path in the words.

The fixed-order staging (SeededPairOrder.write and writeReads, run by fastq trim, quality-trim, adapter-trim, fixed-trim and Viral Recon) reads a bucket whose scratch file is missing as an empty bucket (SeededPairOrder.swift:443, ENOENT returns 0, the same as a bucket no pair fell into), and write returns the pairs counted at the partition (:140-143), never the pairs written. If anything removes a scratch file while the run stages (a cleaner of temporary folders, the user), the staged R1 and R2 silently miss that bucket's pairs, fastp still exits 0 and the trim reads as complete. S3 and not S1 because the run cannot cause it, only an outside deletion of a hidden folder. Count the entries written against the pairs staged in write and writeReads and throw scratchDamaged when they differ, and test it with a bucket file removed between the partition and the drain

The decoy maximum is a measured bound of about one in 1,000 for each barcode, not the stated 1e-6/12 (about 8e-8). In amplicon mate 2 (SRR36291587 R2), the measured worst case, a made 12-barcode one-error kit at the head publishes a false sample in 2.2 to 3.0% of runs (0.19 to 0.25% a barcode on held-out decoys). The 0.4% of the earlier row is the mean over cuts. The stated level on the empirical maximum needs about 1.2 x 10^7 decoys a run, about 860 million index keys. Eight times the decoys (9,600) lower the worst file's rate about 6-fold (0.25% to 0.042%), still about 5,000 times the stated level, and raise the reads a lone real sample needs 8- to 14-fold, to about 1% of an amplicon file. Shotgun cuts stay at margin 2 at every count. A sample sheet already limits the search to the sheet's barcodes (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1240-1250`, `:1268-1282`, `:1338-1345`). The notes line of Stable 2026.11.7 stands (`docs/release-notes/2026.11.7.md:78`): "A barcode not in your pool can still pass as a sample, in about one run in 1,000 for each one and more often in amplicon files, and the summary and the Operations Panel say so."

A read pair judged by organism names, with one mate whose best match shares only the first word of the name of the row and one mate whose best match contradicts the row, now reads Contradicted. Before the BLAST-FIRSTWORD fix the first-word mate counted as supporting, the two mates disagreed and the pair read Ambiguous. The BLAST verification chapter of the manual still says that a hit judged by name agrees when its organism name contains the selected name or the first words of the two names match, and that this older rule counts a different species of the same genus as supporting (`docs/user-manual/chapters/06-classification/06-blast-verification.md:150`). Since the BLAST-FIRSTWORD fix a best match that shares only the first word counts neither for nor against the row, and a name supports the row only when it holds the name of the row as whole words. For linked unanchored lines the floor's sum is 0.0040 against 0.081 to 0.113 of real reads placed at error 0. Since DEMUX-SATKIT the preflight refuses such kits at every error rate unless the person opts in, so the undercount changes no default result, and the row stays S3 since no unanchored line reaches the floor without the opt-in. A later BIO measure (`lge-ruling`) sets a sum that counts these matches.

Measured on whole real reads (BIO-DEMUX-THREE): 95.5% of 8-base barcodes match an amplicon read by chance, up to 73.7% of the reads (SRR36291587, 251 b), and 40.2% match an AT-rich shotgun read, up to 3.05% (SRR12486983, 76 b). effect: Three Cutadapt routes still write linked lines with no anchored side, so cutadapt searches each side anywhere in the read and counts 3 bases of a side at a read end. They are the sample-sheet route of a paired kit (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1268-1308`), which writes `fwd...rc(rev)` and `rev...rc(fwd)` with the bare context (`PlatformAdapterContext.swift:299-305`) and ignores `--location`, and the long-read single and symmetric branches with `linkedSpec` (`:1326`, `:1386`). The sample-sheet route is reached only from sample assignments made in the App (`FASTQOperationDialogState.swift`, `FASTQDerivativeServiceModels.swift`), since the CLI has no sample-sheet option. The same unanchored form on the observed-pair route placed 8.1% to 11.3% of real reads with no barcode at error 0 and 74.0% to 82.2% at 0.15 (cutadapt 5.2). Since DEMUX-SATKIT (413bdd7a1) preflight refuses such lines at every error rate in words, so a person who demultiplexes with a sample sheet in the App sees the refusal, and with Keep Unchecked Samples gets sample files the chance floor did not check. No default run makes a chance sample. A fix anchors these lines as lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR anchored the observed-pair route (`^N{a}first...secondN{b}$`), or exempts a kit only when every line has two sides and every side keeps at least 12 exact bases at its shortest accepted match (`k - floor(e x k) >= 12`, with `k = min(side length, effectiveMinimumOverlap)` and `e = effectiveErrorRate`, BIO-DUAL-TESTS Q2). A `lge-ruling` BIO measure comes first.

Since lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR a custom dual-index file at Both Ends with no sample sheet is searched only at the read ends, and `--max-distance-5prime` and `--max-distance-3prime` (the dialog's 5' Distance and 3' Distance) are the offsets of both strands (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1603-1608` at the lane head 1f0ba32d6). A read of the other strand of a molecule whose two flanks differ has them the other way round, so at 52/47 a molecule with 52 bases before i7 and 47 after i5 gives other-strand reads 47 before and 52 after, which fall outside and go to Unassigned (cutadapt 5.2). The tests build the other-strand read with the forward's flanks, so none catches it. ONT adapters sit at the read start of both strands and are not hit. The notes tell a person to use the longer distance for both. A `lge-ruling` BIO decides whether to mirror the other strand's offsets.

Only the observed-pair route of a custom dual kit caps its Cutadapt lines at 6,000 (lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR). `writeLinkedAdapterFASTA` for built-in dual kits and `writeSingleEndAdapterFASTA` (`DemultiplexingPipeline.swift:1449-1475` at the lane head 1f0ba32d6) write one line for each pair of offsets with no cap, and Cutadapt 5.2 spends about 29 ms a line at `-j 4` before its first read, so a large 5' Distance or 3' Distance makes a run sit for minutes or hours before any read with no words.

Two demultiplex refusals name no fix that works. `noBarcodeAboveChance` (`DemultiplexError.swift:67`) says to check the barcodes and the read end and names no distance, so a person whose barcodes sit in from the read ends reruns at distance 0 and gets the same words. The line cap of lane DEMUX-DUAL-ANCHOR (`:77`) tells a person with more than 3,000 pairs to lower distances that are already 0, where the fix is to split the barcode file, and it names no tool for trimming a known flank (Trim Fixed Bases, Adapter Removal).

The AFFECTED row DEMUX-DUAL-UNANCHORED (`Sources/LungfishWorkflow/Provenance/AffectedResults.swift:460-470`) ends at build 13672, the last build before the refusal 413bdd7a1 (ruling BIO-DUAL-ANCHOR item 12). Preview 2026.11.12 refuses a custom dual-index file at Both Ends with no sample sheet unless the person chooses Keep Unchecked Samples, and a run kept that way still searches each pair anywhere in the read, so its samples can hold chance reads (8 to 11 in 100 at error rate 0 and 74 to 82 in 100 at 0.15 on reads with no barcodes).
